## Two public RFC 8030 urgency types; chat's open UrgencyLevel is used where only the four header values are valid
Crates: jmap-chat-types, jmap-chat-server (vs jmap-types, jmap-web-push)
Evidence: jmap-types/src/push.rs:33 `pub enum Urgency` (closed, documented as "shared by every crate that sends or classifies a push"; re-exported by jmap-web-push/src/lib.rs:48 and scene-server/src/push.rs:20). jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:16 defines a second `pub enum UrgencyLevel { VeryLow, Low, Normal, High, Other(String) }`. It is used in ChatPushCapability.supported_urgency_values (chat-types/src/capability.rs:22,249) and in jmap-chat-server/src/push.rs:267 `pub struct BuiltPush { pub urgency: UrgencyLevel }`, which is the hand-off to jmap-web-push (that crate takes jmap_types::Urgency). RFC 8030 §5.3 closes the set (`urgency-option = "very-low" / "low" / "normal" / "high"`). With Other, an operator can advertise a non-RFC value in supportedUrgencyValues (Session wire), push.rs:125-133 will then accept it, and BuiltPush ends up carrying a value that cannot be mapped to an Urgency header.
Why breaking later: Changing the type of the public fields BuiltPush.urgency and ChatPushCapability.supported_urgency_values, or removing UrgencyLevel or its Other variant, is a semver break.
Fix: Make BuiltPush.urgency and supported_urgency_values use jmap_types::Urgency. Keep an open type only on the client-supplied ChatPushConfig.urgency/mentionUrgency input, where Other is needed to return invalidProperties (chat-push-00 line 126), or reject those at deserialize. Alternatively alias UrgencyLevel to jmap_types::Urgency.
Size: M
